openwrt_wiki.beschreibung: The Enterasys WS-AP3715i is an enterprise Accesspoint normally sold together with a wifi controller, from which it would be configured. Its manufacturer support already ended. OpenWRT liberates it into standalone device with 802.3af POE.
openwrt_wiki.installation:
1. Grab the OpenWrt initramfs, rename it to ap3715.bin. Place it in the root directory of a TFTP server and serve it at `192.168.1.66/24`.

2. Connect to the serial port and boot the AP. Stop autoboot in U-Boot by pressing Enter when prompted. Credentials are identical to the one in the APs interface. By default it is admin / new2day.

3. Alter the bootcmd in U-Boot:

   setenv ramboot_openwrt "setenv ipaddr 192.168.1.1;
   setenv serverip 192.168.1.66; tftpboot 0x2000000 ap3715.bin; bootm"

   setenv boot_openwrt "sf probe 0; sf read 0x2000000 0x140000 0x1000000;
   bootm 0x2000000"

   setenv bootcmd "run boot_openwrt"

   saveenv

4. Boot the initramfs image

   run ramboot_openwrt

5. Transfer the OpenWrt sysupgrade image to the AP using SCP. Install using sysupgrade.

   sysupgrade -n <path-to-sysupgrade.bin>
openwrt_wiki.backup: The manufacturer does not provide a flashable image. To reinstall the OEM firmware, one has to flash a previous backup of the router back on its flash.

openwrt_git.nachricht:
mpc85xx: add support for Enterasys WS-AP3715i

Hardware
--------

SoC:   NXP P1010 (1x e500 @ 800MHz)
RAM:   256M DDR3 (2x Samsung K4B1G1646G-BCH9)
FLASH: 32M NOR (Spansion S25FL256S)
BTN:   1x Reset
WiFi:  1x Atheros AR9590 2.4 bgn 3x3
       2x Atheros AR9590 5.0 an 3x3
ETH:   2x Gigabit Ethernet (Atheros AR8033 / AR8035)
UART:  115200 8N1 (RJ-45 Cisco)

Installation
------------
1. Grab the OpenWrt initramfs, rename it to ap3715.bin. Place it in
   the root directory of a TFTP server and serve it at
   192.168.1.66/24.

2. Connect to the serial port and boot the AP. Stop autoboot in U-Boot
   by pressing Enter when prompted. Credentials are identical to the one
   in the APs interface. By default it is admin / new2day.

3. Alter the bootcmd in U-Boot:

 $ setenv ramboot_openwrt "setenv ipaddr 192.168.1.1;
   setenv serverip 192.168.1.66; tftpboot 0x2000000 ap3715.bin; bootm"

 $ setenv boot_openwrt "sf probe 0; sf read 0x2000000 0x140000 0x1000000;
   bootm 0x2000000"

 $ setenv bootcmd "run boot_openwrt"

 $ saveenv

4. Boot the initramfs image

 $ run ramboot_openwrt

5. Transfer the OpenWrt sysupgrade image to the AP using SCP. Install
   using sysupgrade.

 $ sysupgrade -n <path-to-sysupgrade.bin>

Signed-off-by: David Bauer <mail@david-bauer.net>

installation_guide.Features: 802.11n 3x3 MIMO (3 streams); two single band radios: 5GHz (Radio 1), 2.4GHz (Radio 2); rectangular compact case; two mounting brackets and screws/anchors included; PoE or external 110/240V AC/DC adaptor; dual Ethernet (LAN) ports for fault-tolerant connection and failover; WS-AP3715i 6 internal single-band antennas
installation_guide.Abb. 1-1 Front View: 1 (not used), 2 Console port, 3 External power supply port, 4 LAN port 1, 5 LAN port 2, 6 Reset switch, 7 LEDs, 8 (bottom) Slot for Kensington lock
installation_guide.Rückseite: Mounting slot, Port bay, Mount bracket
installation_guide.LEDs: "four LED indicators" (Front, lower right), aufgezählt 5: 1 AP status (grün an = normal, grün blinkend = Selbsttest/Laden, amber = CPU-/Systemfehler), 2 LAN 1 (grün 100 Mbit/s, amber 1 Gbit/s, aus = kein Link), 3 LAN 2 (wie LAN 1), 4 Radio 2, 5 Radio 1 (grün = an)
installation_guide.Console Port: single RJ45 console port for debug purposes; VT-100 terminal emulator
installation_guide.LAN Port: two 10/100/1000BaseT RJ45 LAN ports; IEEE 802.3/802.3u; The LAN ports also support power over Ethernet (PoE) based on the IEEE 802.3af standard
installation_guide.Reset Switch: press through the hole (located on the top side of the AP) with pen tip; < 5 s: reset; >= 5 s: factory default configuration
installation_guide.Package Contents: 1 WS-AP3715, 2 mounting brackets with screws, 2 wall mounting screws and plastic anchors, 1 Quick Reference card
installation_guide.Montage: Drop ceiling: flat und protruded T-bar bracket; Wall/solid ceiling: 2 Löcher für zwei Schlüssellochschlitze auf der Rückseite, Bohrschablone Abb. 2-4 (mm)
installation_guide.Hinweis Stecker: Lan/Console connectors with shrouds will not fit into the ports. An optional jumper cable may be used or the shroud removed.
installation_guide.Power Connections: PoE through the RJ45 Ethernet port (LAN port) on the top of the AP; or external 12V DC power supply ordered separately; DC-IN port (callout 3); no wall mounts for the 12V DC power supplies
installation_guide.Table A-1: Enclosure material: Metal base, plastic housing; Power source: 802.3af compliant PoE PD, 12V DC input; Power consumption: < 12.94W (Max.); Outside dimensions nur WS-AP3715e: Length 190.5mm, Width 145-180mm, Thickness 29-38mm (ohne Halterung); Antenna (WS-AP3715i only): 6x internal antennas, single band; Uplink Interface: GbE Ethernet x1 with PoE; Radio: IEEE 802.11a/b/g/n, 2.4/5GHz single-band, Dual-radio, 3x3:3 MIMO; Operating temperature 0 to +50 °C
installation_guide.Table A-2 Netzteil: Plastic housing; AC Input 100-240V; DC output 12V; Output current (max) 2A; Output power (max) 24W
installation_guide.Table A-4: WS-AP3715i Indoor MIMO, Single-band: 5 dBi 2.4 GHz, 6 dBi 5 GHz, Connector None

openwrt_hinweis.wert: OpenWrt 24.10 (und damit Gluon 2025.1 ohne Backport): sysupgrade-Image hängt nach "Uncompressing Kernel Image ... OK", weil der simpleImage-Loader auf 0x1100000 gelinkt ist, der uImage-Header aber 0x1500000 nennt; initramfs bootet nur zufällig
openwrt_hinweis.bemerkung: in main seit 2026-04/05 behoben (#23121, 9836f7ca13); 25.12-initramfs wieder zu groß (#25302, Fix #25257 offen); Neanderfunk-Backport mit Loader 0x3000000 ohne Hardwaretest

gluon_seit.bemerkung: Commit 1b6ddac3c6 (2023-09-29, PR #2993); in v2023.1 nicht enthalten; factory = false

installation.wert: seriell + TFTP: initramfs als ap3715.bin vom TFTP-Server 192.168.1.66/24, in U-Boot boot_openwrt/ramboot_openwrt setzen, bootcmd "run boot_openwrt", initramfs booten, dann sysupgrade -n
automatisch per extremeflash (serielles Kabel + LAN, Modell AP3715)
Rettungsweg: serielle Konsole, initramfs per TFTP, dann sysupgrade -n; bei 24.10/2025.1 zuerst initramfs, dann sysupgrade (siehe openwrt_hinweis)

offene_faeden.grund: Quick Reference Card (nicht abgerufen) zeigt evtl. Bohrschablone und Anschlüsse; im abgeschnittenen Installation Guide sind Abbildungen nicht lesbar
Steckermaß der DC-IN-Buchse (Hohlstecker?) in keiner Quelle; vollständige PDF-Fassung (1252522 Byte) suchen oder am Gerät messen

Widerspruch: Abschnitt LAN Port nennt PoE an beiden LAN-Ports, Tabelle A-1 "GbE Ethernet x1 with PoE"; welche Buchse PoE annimmt, am Gerät prüfen (Gluon-Regel: PoE-Eingang = WAN = LAN 1/eth0, nicht belegt)
Konsole nur als "RJ-45 Cisco" beschrieben; Pinbelegung und Pegel (RS-232 oder TTL) in keiner Quelle, Wiki-Abschnitt Serial noch Vorlage
Innenfotos (1 MB) nicht ausgewertet (fccid.io-Abrufe begrenzt); zeigen vermutlich nur das Funkmodul
Label Location (837 KB) nicht ausgewertet; Typenschild aber per Wiki-Foto belegt
Testberichte (DTS 3.6 MB, NII, DFS) mit Leistungswerten je Kette nicht ausgewertet
Richtdiagramme 2.4/5 GHz nur als Grafik im Datenblatt und Installation Guide
Rückseitenfoto im Wiki nur Platzhalter; Platinenfotos fehlen (Seriell intern, Flash-Baustein)

lauf.notiz: Neu erstellt (kein abgebrochener Vorlauf). ToH-Dump + Live-hwdata, OpenWrt-Wiki inkl. Fotos Typenschild/Front, Support-Commit 765f6681 + 7 Folgecommits, DTS/p1010.mk/board.d aus main, Gluon-Target (seit v2023.2) + PR #2993, Forumthread 135834 (OEM-U-Boot-Log), WikiDevi/DeviWiki (nur Funkmodul Senao PCE3300AN), FCC QXO-AP3715I (Modul-Grant: Übersicht, Modul-Handbuch, Außenfotos), Enterasys-Datenblatt 2013 und Installation Guide 9034757-01 (Archiv, abgeschnitten, Text rekonstruiert), extremeflash, Werkstatt-Dokument mpc85xx-simpleimage-loader.md. Innengerät, 802.3af oder 12 V DC 2 A (Netzteil nicht beiliegend), 2x GbE, 2x AR9590 3x3, 6 interne Einband-Antennen, 256 MB RAM, 32 MB SPI-NOR, Konsole außen RJ45 115200 8N1, 567 g, max. 12.8 W. Offen: DC-Steckermaß, welche Buchse PoE nimmt, Konsolen-Pinbelegung/Pegel.
